title: Quarter Tilemap: Signal-driven milestones for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Gabriel Ortega
description: This ticket captures a compact, signal-driven quarterly plan (a 'tilemap') for the Hosted API + Model Catalog initiative. The goal: deliver a prioritized bundle of product work that links OKRs to measurable signals (latency percentiles, unit cost delta, model-usage cohorts). The tilemap approach breaks the quarter into 6 cross-functional tiles (capability + ops + risk control). Each tile contains outcomes, minimum deltas to measure progress, and fallback triggers for canary rollouts. This doc organizes sequencing, staffing, and contingency lanes so engineering and design squads can self-serve sprint slices.
updates: 2026-02-12: Kickoff with Eng, Design, and Infra. Agreed on 6 tiles: Catalog UX, Model Onboarding, Runtime Optimizations, Canary/Rotation Controls, Billing Signals, Observability Dashboards.
2026-02-18: Product/Eng workshop — trade-offs logged: aggressive batching reduces cost but increases tail latency risk; decided to scope batching experiment as opt-in per-model for Q2 tile 3.
2026-02-25: Design supplied low-fidelity flows for catalog UX and a suggested 'tile header' component for console boards. Shared Confluence draft (link below) for feedback.
2026-03-01: Engineering triage — dependencies identified: ENG-1842 (KV cache refactor) and ENG-7340 (continuous-batching rendezvous). Both must land before tile 3 can be completed.
2026-03-03: Reviewed acceptance metrics with Analytics: primary signals are p95 latency, cost-per-1k-tokens, canary error-rate, and model-rotation MTTR. Thresholds appended to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-05: PM review with GTM to align release messaging and customer pilot invites. Selected three early beta customers for tile-by-tile validation. Owners assigned for each tile.

Notes: ongoing blockers include final infra capacity (Dedicated GPU pool allocation) and RBAC edge cases for Private deployments. Working with Security on RBAC audit logging scope (timeline dependency).
acceptance_criteria: Tile headers and roadmap tilemap published in Console (read-only) and Confluence with linked owners and success signals.
Model onboarding flow for two curated models completes end-to-end in staging with documented rollout steps.
Batching experiment (tile 3) demonstrates >=15% unit-cost reduction for dev bucket without increasing p95 latency >10%.
Canary/rotation controls implemented as route-level policy with automatic fallback and documented runbook. Canary error-rate alert triggers before 5% user impact.
Observability dashboards surface token-level cost, per-model latency SLO, and canary health for each tile.
Runbook and customer pilot plan completed and shared with Sales/CS; three pilot customers onboarded with feedback loop.
Dependencies ENG-1842 and ENG-7340 either merged or have clear rollback plans before production traffic ramp.
risks: Capacity risk: Dedicated GPU pool may not be available in desired regions during rollout window; mitigation: schedule region-first rollouts and provide lower-capacity fallback models.
Quality regression: aggressive quantization/batching may reduce output quality on few prompt families; mitigation: add automated eval gating and prompt-level watchlists.
Operational complexity: per-model routing policies increase config surface; mitigation: ship templates and limit initial rollout to curated cohort.
Dependency slippage: if ENG-1842 delayed, tile 3 must shift to research spike; mitigation: plan a parallel lightweight cache shim for limited cohorts.
review_feedback: Design (Caroline Nguyen) asked for clearer CTA on tile headers to request pilot access — added to Console UX scope.
Engineering (Marcus Lee) requested split of tile 3 into 'experiment' and 'harden' phases to reduce release risk — accepted; estimate adjusted.
Security (Amit Patel) requested audit log requirements for model swaps; added to dependency list and security review queue.
Analytics (Priya Rao) recommended adding cohort-level cost attribution to dashboards — prioritized for MVP observability.
Solutions (Lena Ortiz) suggested a customer-facing playbook for 'model fallback' explaining behavior and expected latencies — to be authored before pilot invite.
next_steps: Finalize tile owners and map to sprint lanes for Cycle 2026-W12.
Create sub-issues for each tile (PRD, design tasks, eng spikes).
Lock down Dedicated capacity reservations for pilot regions and confirm with CloudOps.
Open security review ticket for RBAC/audit requirements and schedule 1:1 with Security by 2026-03-12.
Run a pre-mortem on the batching experiment and publish experiment criteria to the team.
